top.line: How to hand keys to paying customers: what Stripe and others do, and a design sealing keys to the buyer's own key.
top.para: Keys as stock, via claim codes.

in-short.line: We sell keys; Stripe stops at payment; others do more; none seals to the buyer; our function; claim codes.

problem.line: Sends, vaults, access keys and cells all end in a key, and our Stripe link stops at the redirect.
problem.para: The hand-over is ours to build.

stripe.line: Stripe gives a reference, a signed webhook, a redirect, products without stock, entitlements and Workflows in preview.
stripe.para: No keys, no stock, no buyer keys.

others.line: FastSpring sells from a key list or calls your server; Paddle Classic did; Lemon Squeezy, Polar, Gumroad generate keys.
others.para: All hold keys in clear; none knows the buyer's key.

design.line: A key pair before checkout, the fingerprint as reference, a Lambda that seals a key from stock, a QR on redirect.
design.para: Only the buyer can open it.

stock.line: Give a provider single-use claim codes to sell and count; the buyer claims, we seal the real key.
stock.para: No provider holds a real key.

now.line: Keep Stripe for money, build the one function, key pairs at checkout, claim codes elsewhere, watch Workflows.

limits.line: Features change and some sources are secondary; the design is not built; fees and tax are separate.

sources.line: Stripe, FastSpring, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Polar and Square documentation, and earlier articles.
